subject: System Design
title: BGP: The Internet's Routing Map
description: A quick win: understand BGP: The Internet's Routing Map.

hook.text: The internet is not one network. It's 70,000 autonomous networks agreeing on how to route traffic.

buildup.text: BGP — Border Gateway Protocol — is how these networks exchange routing information.

discovery.text: Each network announces which IP ranges it can reach. Neighboring networks propagate these announcements.

twist.text: BGP has no built-in security. A misconfigured announcement can hijack traffic for millions of users.

climax.text: BGP is the glue that holds the internet together — and one of its most fragile components.

punchline.text: BGP is the internet's routing map — fragile and critical.

quiz.question: What does BGP do?
options: Exchanges routing information between autonomous networks
Resolves domain names to IP addresses
